candidates.title: Building strong safety evaluations
candidates.summary: 01 Safety first Building strong safety evaluations 01 Safety first 02 Design 03 Run 04 Report 05 Where to start Published Nov 13, 2026 Team Engineering Safety evaluations inform some of the most consequential decisions we make about an AI model, including whether it’s ready to deploy, which safeguards ship alongside it, and what our next round of safety training and research should focus on. When we say a model is “safer than its predecessor,” we mean that it scored better on a set of evals someone built. But a safety claim is only as sound as the eval behind it, and good ones are hard to build. A safety eval measures a model’s propensity to cause or contribute to harm, whether its response to a request makes harm more or less likely, and how severe that harm would be, rather than measuring specific capabilities. It can cover different types of harm. For example, a user may actively request harmful outputs (such as seeking instructions on how to harm themselves), or they may request outputs that are intended to be harmless, but that come with high risk of unintended harm (such as seeking information on the appropriate dose of a drug). Essentially, a safety eval asks, “Given a specific input, did the model do the right thing?” Like other types of evals, these can be tricky to get right: researchers have repeatedly found that AI evals are easy to game , don’t always measure what they claim to measure, and aren’t documented well enough to reproduce . candidates.title: Natural Language Programming: Rethinking Language, Memory, and Cognition in the Era of Generative AI
candidates.summary: Generative Artificial Intelligence is transforming the role of natural language in computational systems. In classical Natural Language Processing (NLP), language was treated as an object of computation: something to analyse, classify, translate, or generate. Large Language Models (LLMs) challenge this perspective, enabling natural language to function increasingly as an executable cognitive medium through which humans structure reasoning, orchestrate problem solving, and regulate hybrid human/AI workflows. This paper introduces Natural Language Programming (NLPg) as a theoretical and epistemological extension of traditional NLP. Rather than focusing on language understanding alone, NLPg conceptualises prompts as dynamic cognitive artefacts that externalise goals, constraints, assumptions, validation criteria, and intermediate reasoning states. Prompting is thus not merely a technical interaction technique, but a form of dialogic cognitive programming operating within distributed human/AI memory architectures. Building on theories of distributed cognition, extended mind, metacognition, and dialogic learning, the paper proposes the notion of Dialogic Working Memory, describing how prompts and conversational states function as temporary external memory structures supporting reasoning continuity and reflective regulation. We further map existing memory architectures (BTMA, SKGE, RMR) onto this framework, illustrating how episodic, semantic, and metacognitive layers support long-horizon conversational coherence. Finally, implications for computational linguistics and AI/mediated knowledge systems are discussed, suggesting a post symbolic and post interface paradigm in which natural language operates simultaneously as communication medium, executable specification, cognitive scaffold, and distributed memory architecture.

candidates.title: 企业 AI Native 研发流程升级与重塑
candidates.summary: 整理自阿里巴巴 Qoder 高级技术专家宋文龙（闻可）8 月 在 AICon 2026 深圳站的 分享《企业 AI Native 研发流程升级与重塑》。他结合自身团队用 Coding Agent 开发 Coding Agent 的实践，以及多家企业客户的落地经验，系统讨论了 Coding Agent 从个人工具走向团队级生产系统所必须跨越的关键问题。围绕 SPEC 先行、团队级 Harness、Agent team 与组织转型，他给出了从许愿式编程到 on the loop 研发范式的完整推进路径，并分享了高德、闪购以及 Qoder 内部的一手案例。
